The wrap rule the stylesheet already carries (394-399) is scoped to four card classes and does not name this list, for the reason its own comment gives — a blanket wrap reaches table cells. Measured independently by the proposer and by the critic in headless Chromium, viewport set by Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride: before the fix documentElement.scrollWidth 1672, li scrollWidth 1629, li right edge 1672, computed overflow-wrap 'normal' on li, strong and span, three page-level offenders (LI@1672, STRONG@1655, SPAN@1655); after the one declaration scrollWidth equal to clientWidth at 320, 375 and 414, computed 'anywhere' on li / strong / span, zero offenders. (2) TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE DEFECT, one missing abstraction, in EIGHT places. test/web/pages.test.js reads src/web/styles.css at lines 345, 359, 1633, 1653, 1693, 1757, 1802 and 1819 and builds its own selector / body / declaration regex at each. validated_work_order.approach:
Two files. One declaration in the stylesheet, and one abstraction in the test file that every stylesheet pin in it then uses — so that at the end of this change there is no second CSS parser left in the suite.

A. Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere;` to the EXISTING `.awaiting-list li` rule in src/web/styles.css, in place among its display / gap / border / radius / padding declarations, with one comment in the same voice and for the same reason as the wrap rule at styles.css:385-393: a grid item is floored at its min-content width, the decision_id is free text, `anywhere` rather than `break-word` because break-word creates the break opportunity but leaves intrinsic sizing alone. NOT as a second rule with the same selector — the new pin's conflict check would read the fix as an override of itself.

B. Add four shared helpers near the top of test/web/pages.test.js, beside H1_HOOK and mainOf, and route all eight stylesheet read sites through them, keeping every existing assertion and every existing failure message verbatim. Only the plumbing moves. The fourth helper is new to this revision and exists to make the migration countable rather than assertable-by-spelling; see AC-9.

  `readStylesheet()` — the single readFileSync of src/web/styles.css, returning `cssRules(source)`. One read site, so 'is the migration complete' is a question about one call rather than about eight regexes.

  `cssRules(source)` — strip /* */, then walk with a brace stack. A frame whose selector starts with '@' is a BLOCK whose children are rules; any other frame is a rule whose body is declarations. ';' terminates a declaration inside a rule and a prelude inside an at-rule, and terminates the accumulated prelude in both cases. Nested rules are emitted with their own selector and a nested flag meaning 'not at top level'. At-rule frames are not emitted. Every rule carries a source index. Against the shipped stylesheet: 68 rules in source order, eight not at top level, being the forced-colors `#main:focus`, the `0%` and `100%` @keyframes steps, `.skeleton`, `#journal-drawer`, `.journal-filters .journal-filter-control`, `.kpi-strip` and `#main`. The keyframe steps are harmless because every lookup is an exact selector match, and the comment must say so, because a later reader who meets them cold will reasonably assume they are a bug. Two failure modes produce plausible output and neither shows up until a pin depends on it: accumulating the prelude through a rule body concatenates `width: 100vw;` onto the selector of the next nested rule (the proposer first measured 73 rules and three mangled selectors this way), and a reader that appends nested text to the parent body instead of descending into it drops every nested rule and reinstates the at-rule blind spot exactly, while passing every test in the file as written today.

  `declarations(body, prop)` — one property's values from an already comment-stripped body, anchored on a declaration boundary (start of body, or after a ';') rather than a bare substring, with a trailing chunk after the last ';' treated as a declaration. THE REASON FOR THE ANCHORING is the measured one, not the elegant one, and it is not the one an earlier round gave, which is a false non-reason: 'min-width' is not a substring of 'min-height' (min-w against min-h), and every pin in the file searches `min-width`, not `width`. The reasons that are real, both green today: (a) a rule with no min-width at all but a comment naming one reads as ['16ch'], count 1, green — the BUG-1 state passing the BUG-1 pin, because the min-width pin does not strip comments while the card pin beside it does; (b) a comment standing beside a real declaration is consumed as the declaration, so widths comes back ['20ch']. Name the custom-property case as the third thing the boundary buys: a bare substring search matches `--min-width: 16ch` and a boundary-anchored one does not, in a stylesheet whose `:root` declares seventeen custom properties. The trailing-chunk clause is a STATED LOOSENING, not a repair: dropping the trailing semicolon from `.page-title`'s `line-height: 1.25` and from `#main > *`'s `min-width: 0` is RED today, because both regexes require the ';'. Nothing is silently removed; the file shouts. A helper that cannot read a body whose last declaration has no semicolon is not a CSS reader, and tests[] pins both directions.

  `conflictingOverrides(rules, pinned, selectors, prop)` — the card pin's override loop, lifted out of that test's body and corrected. The property is a fourth argument and the filter `declarations(other.body, prop).length > 0` runs inside, because the card pin's existing /overflow-wrap\s*:/ filter is what makes the comment above it true — a rule that cannot override the card classes does not turn the suite red. Take the property away and you get one of two failures: drop the filter and a narrow-viewport padding tweak on a pinned selector turns the suite red for a declaration that cannot change the property, re-breaking a tolerance #71 added on purpose; or hardcode overflow-wrap inside and the non-wrap pins get a check that can never fire. `pinned` is the rule or the SET of rules the calling pin has already asserted on, and every member is exempt — the new pin's collection is a set, and without the exemption the fix is reported as an override of itself. A conflict is reported for any rule other than the pinned set, at ANY source index, top-level or nested, declaring `prop` on a comma-split selector part equal to a member of `selectors`. Symmetric in source order, because an override authored above the pinned rule wins at narrow viewports exactly as one below does, and the shipped forced-colors carve-out is the one existing case of that shape.

  THE SELECTOR LOOKUP MUST ANCHOR ON THE SELECTOR'S END — compare a comma-split part to the pinned selector with `===`, never `selector.includes(pinnedSelector)`. '.opportunity-roww' and '.tenant-names' both contain their pinned selector as a substring; the current `\s*\{` anchors give the pins their rename protection today, and a substring lookup deletes it across all eight pins at once, invisibly.

  WHERE THE CONFLICT CHECK IS CALLED, and this is the design decision that matters most. Call it at the card pin (1693) and at the new .awaiting-list pin ONLY. 1655 (#main > *), 1663 (.table-scroll), 1759 (.approval-actions), 1766 (.approval-actions input), 1803 (.journal-drawer-body) and 1820 (.tenant-name) each already collect EVERY rule matching their selector and assert the property on every one of them, so their every-match loop IS the same coverage a same-selector conflict check would give — and because the helper exempts the pinned set, and the pinned set on those six is every rule that could ever match, the call can never fire there. It is dead code that reads as coverage. Put one line in each of those six tests' comments saying the every-match loop is that selector's override check, so the absence reads as a decision. Add one case to the contract test distinguishing a pin whose pinned set is the whole selector from one whose pinned set is a single rule, so the distinction cannot rot silently.

  TWO PINS THAT ARE NOT MECHANICAL. .page-title asserts EVERY .page-title rule rather than the first: an appended `.page-title { margin: 4rem }` is green under a first-match check and the page breaks. #main:focus needs an exact count, not a conflict check, because the conflict check is genuinely unavailable there: its one later same-selector rule IS the intentional forced-colors carve-out, so any same-selector override check reports it by design. The pin asserts exactly one top-level #main:focus rule, which declares `outline: none`, and exactly one rule not at top level, which is the carve-out. Those land at source indices 14 and 15. An appended third rule is red on the count, and the carve-out does not move the count because it is nested rather than a second top-level rule.

  THE FORCED-COLORS PIN, the third place that needs care, and the loosening is accepted on purpose and pinned. The current regex at pages.test.js:360 is /@media\s*\(forced-colors:\s*active\)\s*\{[^@]*?#main:focus\s*\{([^}]*)\}/, and its `[^@]*?` means it only finds the carve-out when it is the first thing in the block. The reader finds it wherever it sits, so the rewrite is strictly MORE PERMISSIVE. The assertions that carry the meaning are unchanged — the carve-out exists, declares `outline: 2px solid CanvasText`, and comes after the bare #main:focus rule at equal specificity, both selectors being 1,1,0 — and a mutation that puts another nested rule before the carve-out must still pass, so the loosening is a stated behaviour. The test's comment says the parser's strictness changed, not the assertion. Keep the `length > 0` guard on the not-at-top-level lookup specifically, so a reader regression that stopped descending into at-rules cannot make this test pass vacuously on a file with no carve-out at all. The source-order assertion at pages.test.js:372-377 is the only thing in the suite that pins WHY the carve-out wins, and its comment says so; it must survive the rewrite as a comparison of source INDICES rather than character offsets, deliberately, not by accident.

  THE NEW .awaiting-list li PIN, in the house style of #main > * and .tenant-name rather than a whole-body assertion, and in ONE test. In order: (a) collect every rule that is NOT nested, whose comma-split selector part is `.awaiting-list` or `.awaiting-list li`, and whose body declares overflow-wrap — the property filter is part of the COLLECTION predicate, not only inside the helper, and the test's comment must say that in those terms, because the media-nested rule's selector part IS exactly '.awaiting-list li' and an unfiltered collection takes it in, at which point deepEqual([], ['anywhere']) fails and the suite goes red for a padding declaration; (b) require the collection to be NON-EMPTY, with a message that says so, so deleting the declaration and leaving a comment is red; (c) require each collected rule's overflow-wrap values to deepEqual ['anywhere']; (d) run `conflictingOverrides(rules, collected, ['.awaiting-list', '.awaiting-list li', '.awaiting-list li strong', '.awaiting-list li span'], 'overflow-wrap')` and require it to report nothing. Today the file yields exactly one `.awaiting-list li` rule with zero overflow-wrap declarations in it, so (b) is what turns the current state red rather than vacuous. TWO ADDITIONS TO THE PROPOSAL, both from the critique: `.awaiting-list` (the ul) is in the collection's selector set, because `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the parent is inherited by the li, removes its min-content floor identically and fixes the page — the pin must not report a correct fix as absent; and the collection requires the declaration to be at TOP LEVEL, because a fix authored only inside `@media (max-width: 900px)` satisfies the new pin in full AND satisfies the whole browser sweep at 320/375/414, all of which are inside that query, while the defect is not inherently narrow-viewport. Both additions have a cost and both are recorded in out_of_scope: a deliberately media-scoped fix reads as absent, and a rule declaring overflow-wrap twice reads red on the second value.

  (e) the render half, in the same test, AS A LINK ASSERTION AND NOTHING MORE. Use `seededRepos(prefix)` — which creates tenant_demo and the three pending approvals — NOT bare `freshRepos()`, which has no tenant and makes `decisionsOf` return [] so the page renders the empty branch with no `class="awaiting-list"` at all. Create one decision whose decision_id is 140 unbreakable characters through the decisions repository on top, and assert that /journal at override 'partial' emits class="awaiting-list" and an `<li data-decision-id=...>` whose `<strong>` holds that id whole. The assertion is that the selector is a fact about the page and the id is not truncated in the data layer. It is NOT a measurement of layout and must not be described as one: the renderer reads no stylesheet, the repository has no browser driver, and this half passes with or without the declaration. The 140-character id is kept because it makes the selector's purpose legible to the next reader, not because its length is doing work; the test's comment must say so in those terms. The half does NOT assert 'and nothing else': .journal-drawer-body already carries overflow-wrap alongside four other declarations in one rule, and a whole-body assertion would force the fix into a second `.awaiting-list li` rule whose duplicate selector the conflict check reads as an override of itself.

  ONE CONTRACT TEST for the helpers, driven by fixture strings rather than the shipped stylesheet: a comment-only min-width reads as no declarations; an at-rule-nested rule carries its own selector and a nested flag; a later same-selector rule declaring an UNRELATED property (e.g. `padding: var(--space-3)`) is not a conflict; a media-nested overflow-wrap override IS a conflict; an override authored ABOVE the pinned rule IS a conflict; '.opportunity-roww' does not match '.opportunity-row'; a pin that collects a SET exempts every member of it from its own conflict check; and a pin whose pinned set is the whole selector is distinguishable from one whose pinned set is a single rule. The eight-pin migration otherwise has no automated guard on its own plumbing — every proof it works is a mutation a reviewer runs by hand, and the helpers will outlive this ticket.

C. Fix the pre-existing red test, because nothing else in this change is verifiable while it is red: AC-3 and AC-5 both read the file's totals. The assertion at pages.test.js:1779 is /<li class="approval-card">/ and the markup at pages.js:1043 is `<li class="approval-card" data-testid="approval-card" data-approval-card ...>` — a qa/selectors.md-stable data-testid was added to the element after the matcher was written, and the matcher anchors on the closing '>'. The fix is /<li class="approval-card"[\s>]/, which takes the file to 72/72/0. `\b` does not work and the reason is worth a comment: after the closing quote both the quote and the following space are non-word characters, so there is no boundary there. While in that helper, drop the `approval.requested` raw-event append from pendingApprovalRepos — grep across src/, test/ and scripts/ finds exactly two hits, the helper's own docstring and the append — and rewrite the docstring to say what is actually true: the approval cards come from the seed's three SEEDED_PENDING_IDS, written through the approvals repository at scripts/seed.js:579, not from a raw event. The existing docstring's cited evidence is also wrong: it points at 'the read at src/web/pages.js:924' and that line is experiment-card markup (pages.js:920-926). Do not write 'four pending' anywhere — three pending, four seeded, one lapsed. tests[] now carries the removal as a stated mutation rather than prose.

AC-9 is rewritten to assert the migration structurally — one readFileSync, inside a new readStylesheet() helper, and three named helper calls — and the four scans by pattern. No line number appears anywhere in this order.

AC-5 claimed twelve mutations go red and eight of them do. I read the new pin's own check text in AC-4 and the pin it specifies in files[] (6): the collection filters on overflow-wrap, the assertion is that property's values, the conflict check filters on the same property. `display`, `padding` and `border` are named nowhere, and the render half is HTML containment. I took the critique's SECOND option, not its first, and the reason is in alternatives_considered: widening a defect pin to police the display model and the padding of a rule the ticket is not fixing couples the fix to four declarations the defect has nothing to do with, and their cost is a test that goes red on a cosmetic edit with a message about overflow. The render half was wrong twice over, and both halves of the critique hold. It is red on arrival — `freshRepos()` creates no tenant, `decisionsOf` returns [] for one (src/web/pages.js:614-619), and the page renders the empty branch with no awaiting list at all; the precedent the order cites does not transfer, because the tenant-name test at pages.test.js:1818 calls `freshRepos()` and then creates its tenant. Five more folded in. WHAT I REJECTED, and it is the one place I part company with the critique — its finding 10, on its premise and not its conclusion. It claims the three `li.approval-card` at /approvals are 'not offenders at all' on a runner with overlay scrollbars, and I dismiss that: the proposer measured 309 against 305 on this same runner, the critic measured clientWidth equal to innerWidth under its own CDP override, and I could not reproduce either without booting a browser. A pre-existing 4px overflow appearing and disappearing with the scrollbar setting is exactly the claim two earlier rounds of this plan inverted, and I will not delete a measured defect on a platform setting I could not reproduce. I took the fix the finding asks for, which is right whichever of us is right about the machine: name the permitted offenders by selector and carry no pixel. A criterion that violates its own instruction to 'read the invariant, not the literals' is a defect in the criterion, and the selector does the same work as the numbers did. I also declined the critique's first option on the `.awaiting-list` mutations and its option to drop the render half outright, and declined its request to pin `cssRules(stylesheet).length === 68`, which would not have caught either of the two reader bugs actually observed.

WHERE I DIFFER FROM THE BRIEF. Once, and it is small. The brief's `required` said the `grep -c 'css\.matchAll\|stripped\.matchAll\|body\.matchAll'` -> 0 check was 'already correct' and should be kept. It counts a variable name, and this order names a helper parameter `body`, so a correct implementation of the order's own specification — `[...body.matchAll(/(?:^|;)\s*min-width\s*:\s*([^;]*)/g)]`, the natural boundary-anchored form — fails it. I dropped it as an assertion and kept the thing the brief actually wanted underneath it: a check a wholly-unmigrated file cannot fake. The structural check cannot be faked either and cannot be broken by the order's own vocabulary. The brief recorded no decision this contradicts; its 'Decided for this issue' section is empty.

WHAT NOBODY HAS RESOLVED, and it is the same thing the last two rounds said. The migration is unexecuted. Three independent prototypes agree on the reader's output — 68 rules, eight nested, #main:focus at 14 and 15 — and agreement is corroboration, not proof, and not one of them was ever run as the file that will ship. The blast radius if the reader is wrong is every stylesheet assertion in a 1900-line test file, which is why the contract test exists, why the `length > 0` guards stay, and why the first instruction in both this order's unknowns and its tests[] is to run the matrix against the real helpers before doing anything else. My confidence is in the fix and in the reasoning; it is not in the plumbing, and the order says so rather than rounding it up.
